tasks.short: Hold supervision sessions, read and comment on drafts, contact internship hosts, keep progress forms, and send internship assessments to the internship office.

steps.what: Arts teacher supervises undergraduate or graduate teaching, internship and research work in supervision sessions
Arts teacher reads and comments on students' drafts
Arts teacher visits or calls internship hosts
Arts teacher fills in progress forms and supervision logs: on paper and by e-mail today, in the placement system with dates and host details already there after the change
Arts teacher checks the final internship assessment: it fits the host's feedback, the drafts and the progress forms
Arts teacher submits the checked internship assessment to the internship office: by e-mail today, from the placement system after the change

tasks.design: Internships and theses are tracked in the school's placement system ({OTHER}) with milestones, so progress forms are filled in once with the dates and host details already there. Once the teacher has completed and checked the assessment, the teacher submits it to the internship office from the same system. Supervision sessions, commenting on drafts and contact with hosts stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress forms were paper or e-mail attachments sent back and forth.
tasks.enabler_now: Placement systems track milestones and route assessments.
tasks.still_hard: Hosts rarely fill in forms on time.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a student through a creative block in their final project.
tasks.altitude: Less copying and mailing of forms; supervision stays.

evidence.claim: Placement systems can track internship milestones and route assessments to the office.

assumptions: Boundary: from the supervised students to the submitted assessment; final grading by the exam board is outside.
Input contract: placement details from the internship office; fallback is paper forms and e-mail.
Supervision and commenting do not change.
Students' and hosts' time does not change.
s4 keeps 70 because only dates and host details stop being copied, the progress notes are still written; s5 keeps 50 for submitting from the system.
research_questions: Are assessments submitted on time more often?

incremental.description: Arts teacher updates milestones when placements change.

approvals.approved_version: The internship assessment exactly as checked by the teacher in s4b, submitted once to the internship office from the placement system; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: placement details are often missing in the system, so s4 keeps 90 (2.5); high: details present as assumed (4.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Chair department meetings, prepare agendas and minutes, plan teaching assignments, answer requests from the faculty office, approve budget requests, and send minutes to staff.

steps.what: Arts teacher chairs department meetings as department head
Arts teacher writes the minutes and action list
Arts teacher plans teaching assignments for department staff
Arts teacher performs administrative duties such as answering requests from the faculty office
Arts teacher approves budget requests from staff
Arts teacher checks the final minutes: decisions and actions say what the meeting agreed, with owners
Arts teacher shares the checked minutes with department staff from the document space

tasks.design: Agendas and minutes follow a shared template with standing items and an action list in the document space ({DOCS}); once the head has finished and checked the minutes, the head shares them with staff from there. A teaching-load planner adds up hours per staff member from the course catalogue and contracts, so the head sees overloads before assigning. Standard answers to recurring faculty requests sit on a shared page. Chairing meetings and approving budgets stay with the head.
tasks.previous_blocker: Minutes, teaching loads and requests were handled by hand and by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared templates and load planners are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching assignments involve personal wishes and history.
tasks.human_edge: Settling a dispute between two colleagues over a course.

evidence.claim: Teaching-load planners can add up contact hours per staff member from course data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the meeting agenda and requests to minutes shared; faculty-level decisions are outside.
Input contract: course hours from the catalogue; contract hours from HR; fallback is spreadsheets and e-mail.
Chairing and approving budgets do not change.
Staff read minutes as they do today.

s2 keeps 85 because the template gives standing items and layout, the head still writes the minutes; s3 keeps 60 for deciding assignments; s4 keeps 80 for requests the page does not cover; s6 keeps 30 for sharing.
research_questions: Do teaching overloads get caught before the term?

incremental.description: Arts teacher keeps the standard answers page current.

approvals.approved_version: The minutes with decisions and actions exactly as checked by the department head in s2b, shared once with department staff from the document space; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: contract hours are not available from HR, so loads are still added up by hand and s3 keeps 85 (11.0); high: planner fed as assumed (16.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search literature and archives, conduct research or creative practice, write the article or chapter, format references, check the manuscript, submit it, and answer reviewers.

steps.what: Arts teacher searches literature and archives for the research question
Arts teacher conducts research in the field through practice, archives and analysis
Arts teacher writes the findings for professional journals or books
Arts teacher formats references and the manuscript to the journal's style
Arts teacher checks the final manuscript: findings, quotes and references are right
Arts teacher submits the manuscript through the journal's portal
Arts teacher answers reviewers' comments and revises the manuscript
Arts teacher checks the final revision and response letter: each reviewer point is answered
Arts teacher resubmits the checked revision through the journal's portal

tasks.design: Library database alerts and saved searches bring new sources on the teacher's topics, and a reference manager imports them by DOI with notes. The same reference manager formats citations and the reference list in each journal's style. Research, writing, checking, submitting and answering reviewers stay with the teacher; no model writes the findings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources were searched again for each project and references formatted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Reference managers import by DOI and format to journal styles.
tasks.still_hard: Archives and performance recordings in the arts are often not in databases.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the forgotten score in an archive box that changes the argument.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and formatting; research stays.

reach.learn: Whether saved searches find more sources.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI gives topic summaries and points to foundational papers.
Reference managers import references by DOI and format them to journal styles.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research question to the revision sent; editing by the publisher is outside.
Input contract: database access from the library; fallback is manual searching and formatting.
Research, writing and reviewing do not change.
Journals accept reference styles from reference managers.
research_questions: Does formatting time per submission fall?

incremental.description: Arts teacher corrects references the import got wrong.

approvals.approved_version: The manuscript exactly as checked by the teacher in s5, submitted once through the named journal's portal; any change needs a new check.
The revised manuscript and response letter exactly as checked by the teacher in s7b, resubmitted once to the same journal; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: practice-based research with few indexed sources, so alerts help little and s1 keeps 90 (5.5); high: text-based research as assumed (9.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find funding calls, write the project description and standard sections, build the budget, collect letters and signatures, check the proposal with co-applicants, and submit it.

steps.what: Arts teacher finds suitable funding calls
Arts teacher writes the project description of the grant proposal
Arts teacher builds the budget with the research office
Arts teacher writes standard sections such as data management, budget justification and knowledge use

loop.input: The teacher's project description, the budget sheet and the call's section template.
loop.output: Draft standard sections in the funder's template.
loop.check: Code checks every required section is present, length limits hold and every amount in the budget justification matches the budget sheet; the teacher checks that each drafted section says what the project description and budget support, and edits and approves the text.
loop.stop: Stops when the checks pass and the teacher approves, or after two failed redrafts the teacher writes the section.
loop.why_not_simpler: Standard sections must describe each project; a template only gives the headings.

steps.what: Arts teacher collects letters of support and signatures by e-mail
Arts teacher checks the full proposal with co-applicants: description, budget, sections and letters match the call and what was agreed
Arts teacher submits the proposal through the funder's portal

tasks.design: The research office sends funding alerts matched to the teacher's profile. A budget template holds the funder's rates, so totals are computed. A bounded step drafts the standard sections from the teacher's own project description and the budget; code checks sections, length limits and amounts, and the teacher edits the text. Letters are signed electronically ({ESIGN}). The project description, the check with co-applicants and submitting stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every proposal's standard sections and budget were written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft standard sections; budget templates hold funder rates.
tasks.still_hard: Funders judge the idea, which no draft improves.
tasks.human_edge: Framing an artistic project so a science funder sees its value.
tasks.altitude: The teacher edits standard sections instead of writing them.

reach.learn: Whether proposals reach the office earlier.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft standard proposal sections from a project description.
NWO referees may not use generative AI, and uploading a proposal to such a tool breaches confidentiality.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research idea to the proposal submitted; the funder's review is outside.
Input contract: funder templates and rates from the research office; fallback is writing from scratch.
The project description and the co-applicant check stay with the teacher.
Only the teacher's own text goes into the drafting step, never others' proposals.

s3 keeps 60 because rates and totals are computed but planning costs stays; s4 keeps 60 because drafts give a start but the teacher rewrites each section for the project; s5 keeps 60 for chasing letters.
research_questions: How much of the drafted sections does the teacher change?

already_counted.description: Arts teacher edits and approves drafted standard sections.

incremental.description: Arts teacher checks the funder's rules on AI use for each call.

approvals.approved_version: The proposal with description, budget, sections and letters exactly as checked with co-applicants in s6, submitted once through the funder's portal for this call; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: drafts need much rewriting and the template lacks this funder's rates, so s4 and s3 keep 80 (13.0); high: drafts and template as assumed (20.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The arts teacher keeps supervising, chairing, researching and writing the core of proposals; paper forms, hand-built loads, reference formatting and standard sections shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who spends saved time on artistic research.

job.title: Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary
